prompts:
Use case: stylized-concept
Create archer-a.png, a production animation sprite sheet for Riley Wheel Brawl 2.0. Use attached Image 1 (master-side.png) as the LOCKED character design and art style reference. Output landscape 1536x1024 with genuinely transparent background, real alpha.
Exactly EIGHT separate full-body drawings in TWO rows of FOUR, reading order left to right then next row. Each cell 384x512; fit whole figure plus tall longbow with margins, clear transparent gaps, no overlap. Equal character scale in all eight cells; heads about y=35 and y=547, boot baseline y=475 and y=987 respectively. Preserve master proportions, normalized to sheet cell size. ALL face LEFT, profile/slight 3/4.
Locked identity: lean adult man 25, narrow alert face, short brown beard and brown hair, white hood UP with visible face, white flowing cloak with brown mud on hem, gold sunburst left breast and gold clasp, brown leather jerkin over gray mail, leather bracers, white-fletched arrows in back quiver, brown trousers, brown boots, short belt knife. Exactly match reference face, garments, colors, ink line quality, shading and bow design. NO shield. Tall wooden longbow with recurved tips of constant length and curve in every frame; only natural flex under draw. Hand-drawn HD 2D fighting game sprite art, confident dark brown/near-black ink outline thicker exterior, thinner interior, clean 2-3 step cel shading with subtle painterly gradients, rich grounded colors; soft upper left key, gentle cool right rim, moderate lighting. Not pixel art, not 3D, not photoreal, not chibi.
TOP ROW WALK LEFT, longbow held LOW in anatomical LEFT hand:
1 left boot forward leftward heel contact, right boot behind, cloak trails gently right.
2 passing phase, rear boot moves through, supporting leg near vertical, weight rises, clearly different from 1.
3 right boot forward leftward contact, left boot behind, alternate stride, clearly different drawing.
4 second passing phase, left boot passes through, weight raised, subtly different cloak folds and leg configuration from 2.
BOTTOM ROW SHOOT, arrow aimed horizontally LEFT:
5 REACH: left hand holds bow in front, anatomical right hand reaches back over right shoulder to retrieve arrow from quiver, open reaching fingers.
6 NOCK: right hand sets white-fletched arrow on string near bow grip, bow rising toward horizontal shooting position, visibly not fully drawn.
7 FULL DRAW: left bow arm fully extended LEFT, right hand pulls string to cheek, arrow perfectly horizontal pointed LEFT, string stretched from tips to cheek. Distinct full draw posture.
8 AIM: still full draw, squinting down horizontal arrow LEFT; subtly settled stance, shoulder and head adjust, a genuinely new drawing following 7, no release.
Every figure has exactly two arms, two legs, two booted feet and anatomically correct five-fingered hands. Keep bow and quiver coherent, no extra weapons. No floor, no ground shadow, no effects, no dust, no motion lines, no text, no labels, no grid, no borders, no frame numbers. Transparent empty space around and between figures. Eight only, four per row.

inspection.note: RGB data retains backdrop colors under zero alpha. Selected third attempt improves bow consistency. Walk poses have limited alternation and bows held upright rather than low; exact design/pose fidelity cannot be guaranteed.
